associations.structural_reason: Every primitive Pythagorean triple is generated by a ternary tree from (3,4,5). The perfect cuboid requires three triples sharing legs — this is a tree intersection problem.
The perfect cuboid asks for a box whose vertex distances are all integers — equivalent to packing integer-radius spheres around the origin in a specific configuration.
Each face diagonal equation is a generalized Pell equation. The system requires simultaneous solutions, which is structurally similar to multi-dimensional continued fraction convergence.

Stabilizer codes require finding simultaneous +1 eigenspaces of commuting operators. The perfect cuboid requires simultaneous integer solutions of commuting quadratic forms — the algebraic structure is parallel.

Nash equilibrium is guaranteed in mixed strategies (reals) but may not exist in pure strategies (integers). The perfect cuboid has solutions over Q (Euler bricks scaled) but possibly not over Z with the space diagonal constraint.
